edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina (PL 1, Paris 1844), De baptismo, via Latin Wikisource transcription
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Non quod in aquis Spiritum sanctum consequamur; sed in aqua emundati sub Angelo, Spiritui sancto praeparamur. Hic quoque figura praecessit. Sic enim Joannes ante praecursor Domini fuit, praeparans vias ejus: ita et Angelus Baptismi arbiter superventuro Spiritui sancto vias dirigit ablutione delictorum, quam fides impetrat, obsignata in Patre, et Filio, et Spiritu sancto. Nam si in tribus testibus stabit omne verbum, quanto magis, dum habemus per benedictionem eosdem arbitros fidei, quos et sponsores salutis, sufficit ad fiduciam spei nostrae etiam numerus nominum divinorum? Cum autem sub tribus, et testatio fidei, et sponsio salutis pignerentur, necessario adjicitur Ecclesiae mentio; quoniam ubi tres, id est Pater et Filius et Spiritus sanctus, ibi Ecclesia, quae trium corpus est.
pass_a_gloss: Not that we obtain the Holy Spirit in the waters; but having been cleansed in the water under the Angel, we are prepared for the Holy Spirit. This figure also went before. For just as John was before a precursor of the Lord, preparing His ways: so also the Angel, the arbiter of Baptism, directs the ways for the Holy Spirit that is to come, by the washing away of sins, which faith obtains, sealed in the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. For if every word stands in three witnesses, how much more, while we have through blessing these same ones as arbiters of faith, and also as sponsors of salvation, is the number of divine names sufficient for the confidence of our hope? But when under three, both the testimony of faith and the sponsorship of salvation are pledged, the mention of the Church is necessarily added; since where there are three, that is the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, there is the Church, which is the body of the three.

choices.why: indicating the role of the Angel in baptism
describing the role of the three divine names
describing the relationship between the Church and the three divine names

pass_b_english: We do not receive the Holy Spirit in the waters; rather, once we have been cleansed in the water under the Angel, we are prepared for the Holy Spirit. This pattern also appeared earlier. Just as John went before the Lord as a forerunner to prepare his ways, so the Angel, the arbiter of Baptism, clears the way for the coming Holy Spirit through the washing away of sins—a washing that faith obtains, sealed in the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. If every word stands on the testimony of three witnesses, how much more does the very number of the divine names guarantee our confident hope, now that we possess those same three as guarantors of our faith and sponsors of our salvation through the blessing? And when both the profession of faith and the pledge of salvation are made under those three, the mention of the Church becomes unavoidable; for where the three are—that is, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—there is the Church, which is the body of the three.

review.notes: The translation accurately reflects the Latin text. Pass A and Pass B both correctly handle the complex syntax of the second half of the paragraph. Pass B's stylistic choices (e.g., 'clears the way' for 'dirigit vias' and 'unavoidable' for 'necessario') remain faithful to the sense of the Latin. No scripture citations were present in the source to verify.
